title: How Trump's Tariffs Got a Reality Check
summary: Explainer on the Supreme Court striking down the IEEPA tariffs: costs fell on US importers and customers, the trade deficit barely moved, manufacturing jobs fell, and refunds threaten the budget.

assertions.quote: the foreign exporters aren't eating the tariffs. They're 90-95% passed through to US importers and their customers.
Trump had promised that foreign countries would be the ones paying for its tariffs, but ...
It was almost exactly the same size as the trade deficit that it had in 2024.

verdicts.note: The 2025 goods deficit was roughly unchanged at about $1.2 trillion as trade shifted from China to Mexico and Asia.

assertions.quote: reshuffle trade away from China and towards Mexico and other Asian countries more than reducing the aggregate trade deficit

verdicts.note: Customs data show China's share of US imports fell while Mexico, Vietnam and others rose.

China's share of U.S. non-oil imports fell another 5 points to below 10 percent in January-November 2025 while Mexico and Vietnam gained the most share; the post documents the shift but says nothing about whether total imports fell.

assertions.quote: in the last year, the US lost more than 80,000 manufacturing jobs. That's even as these tariffs went into place.

verdicts.note: Manufacturing employment hit a recent low in December 2025 according to BLS, so it declined over 2025; the 72,000 recovery since then is a 2026 development and the release says nothing about tariffs as the cause.

assertions.quote: if those imported components and big things that they use like steel and aluminum are more expensive as a result of tariffs, they can't hire
any growth that was there was really driven by the lower-tariffed industries, things like pharmaceuticals, electronics.

verdicts.note: Industrial production split by tariff exposure showed autos and metals lagging pharma and electronics in 2025.

assertions.quote: The principle driver of that trend is not trade, it's technology.

verdicts.note: Automation explains most of the long-run decline, but China-shock studies attribute a substantial share of 2000s losses to trade.

assertions.quote: the administration was really counting on this revenue from the tariffs to plug that fiscal hole

verdicts.note: Duties collected lifted the average duty rate to around 8.5 percent of import value while 86 to 94 percent of the tariff incidence fell on U.S. importers, so import prices for tariffed goods rose about 11 percent more than untariffed ones; revenue and higher U.S. costs arrive together.
